;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[North East Delhi riots]]
**Violent clashes between [[Hinduism in India|Hindu]] and [[Islam in India|Muslim]] protesters over the [[Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019|Citizenship Amendment Act]] continue in [[North East Delhi]], [[India]], leaving 27 people dead and at least 180 injured. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/pm-narendra-modi-tweets-appeal-to-my-sisters-and-brothers-of-delhi-to-maintain-peace-and-brotherhood-2185982 (NDTV)]
*[[Syrian civil war]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–present)]], [[Turkish involvement in the Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Turkey]]'s [[Ministry of National Defense (Turkey)|MoD]] says two [[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkish]] troops were killed in an [[airstrike]] in [[Syria]]'s [[Idlib Governorate]]. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20200226-two-turkish-soldiers-killed-in-air-strikes-in-syrias-idlib/ (Middle East Monitor)]
**[[Turkey]]'s MoD claims 114 [[Syrian Army]] troops were "neutralized" in retaliation. An air defense system, a [[ZU-23-2]] [[Anti-aircraft warfare|AA gun]], an [[Anti-tank warfare|antitank weapon]], 3 [[Tank|Tanks]], an ammunition vehicle and 2 [[Military engineering vehicle|engineering vehicles]] were destroyed while 3 tanks were captured. [https://www.aksam.com.tr/guncel/son-dakika-haberi-msb-idlibde-2-askerimiz-sehit-oldu-114-rejim-askeri-etkisiz-hale-getirildi/haber-1048511 (''Akşam'')]

;Arts and culture
*Bob Weighton, aged 111, of [[Alton, Hampshire|Alton]], [[Hampshire]], [[England]], is named the [[Oldest people|oldest living man in the world]] after the death of Chitetsu Watanabe of [[Japan]] at the age of 112. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2020/feb/26/britains-bob-weighton-becomes-oldest-man-in-the-world (''The Guardian'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
***102 more coronavirus cases are confirmed in [[Italy]], bringing the number to 424. Another virus-related death is confirmed, bringing the death toll in the country to 12. [https://tg24.sky.it/cronaca/2020/02/26/coronavirus-ultime-notizie-diretta.html (Sky Tg24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
***In [[Josefstadt]], [[Vienna]], students at [[Albertgasse high school]] have been prohibited from leaving the school after one of their instructors was flagged as potentially carrying the virus since he had recently returned from a trip to [[Northern Italy]]. [https://www.rt.com/news/481723-austria-school-coronavirus-lockdown/ (RT)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
*** In [[California]], [[San Francisco]] declares a public emergency. [[Santa Clara County, California|Santa Clara]] and [[San Diego County, California|San Diego]] counties have made similar declarations. [https://www.news.com.au/lifestyle/health/health-problems/coronavirus-outbreak-in-the-united-states-now-inevitable-health-official-warns/news-story/78637c83a02bb5e314e68e34bfa8a017 (News AU)]
**The first case in [[Latin America]] is confirmed by the [[Ministry of Health (Brazil)|Ministry of Health]] of [[Brazil]] in [[São Paulo]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/china-coronavirus-outbreak-latest-updates-200226003835539.html (Al Jazeera)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
***[[Greece]] confirms its first case in [[Thessaloniki]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-greece/greece-confirms-first-coronavirus-case-idUSKCN20K1IA?feedType=RSS&feedName=worldNews (Reuters)]
**[[Romania]] and [[Georgia (Country)|Georgia]] report their first cases. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-virus-romania/romania-confirms-first-case-of-coronavirus-health-minister-idUSKCN20K370 (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-georgia/georgia-reports-first-coronavirus-case-in-the-country-health-minister-idUSKCN20K2SY (Reuters)]
**A 62-year-old man in [[Seville]] becomes the first non imported infected case of coronavirus in [[Spain]]. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/local/sevilla/20200226/473797279023/confirmado-primer-positivo-coronavirus-sevilla-andalucia.html?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_content=local (''La Vanguardia'')] 

;Law and crime
*Six prisoners are shot dead by [[Papua New Guinea Police]] as they escape from prison in [[Western Highlands Province]]. They were among 100 inmates who escaped during a mass breakout. Scores of others are captured. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/410354/six-prisoners-shot-dead-in-mass-jailbreak-in-png (RNZ)]
*[[Germany]] repeals its 2015 ban on advertisements for professional [[assisted suicide]] practices, after finding that its prohibition violated the [[Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany|German Constitution]]. [[Euthanasia#Passive and active euthanasia|Passive human euthanasia]] itself has been [[Legality of euthanasia#Germany|legal]] in the republic since 2014. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51643306 (BBC News)]
*[[Milwaukee brewery shooting]]
**Six people, including the shooter, are killed in a [[Mass shootings in the United States|mass shooting]] at the [[Molson Coors Beverage Company]] in [[Milwaukee]], [[Wisconsin]], United States. The perpetrator, who [[Murder-suicide|committed suicide]], was an employee who was [[dismissal (employment)|fired]] earlier in the day. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/02/26/acritical-incident-reported-molsoncoors-milwaukee-campus/4884534002/ (''USA Today'')] [https://wgntv.com/2020/02/26/milwaukee-police-responding-to-critical-incident-at-miller-coors-headquarters/ (WGN-TV)]
*The [[Donald Trump 2020 presidential campaign|re-election campaign]] of [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] files a libel suit against ''[[The New York Times]]'' over a 2019 [[Op-ed|editorial piece]] that accused the Trump campaign of [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections|striking a deal with Russia]] during the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 presidential election]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-election-trump/trump-campaign-says-it-is-suing-new-york-times-over-russia-opinion-piece-idUSKCN20K2X3?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**The [[Government of Spain|Spanish]] and [[Generalitat of Catalonia|Catalan government]] meets for the first time after breaking the talks one year ago in the named "Dialogue Board" as a way to solve the constitutional and political crisis between both governments that erupted in 2017. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20200226/473795483461/constitucion-mesa-dialogo-gobierno-generalitat-catalunya-pedro-sanchez-quim-torra-ultimas-noticias-hoy-en-directo.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
*[[Lynching in the United States]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] votes 410–4 to pass the [[Emmett Till]] Antilynching Act, which designates [[lynching]] a [[Federal crime in the United States|federal crime]]. This is the first time that anti-lynching legislation has ever passed [[United States Congress|Congress]]. [https://www.npr.org/2020/02/26/809705702/it-s-about-time-house-approves-historic-bill-making-lynching-a-federal-crime (NPR)]

;Science and technology
*Astronomers at the [[Catalina Sky Survey]] in [[Arizona]], [[United States]], say an object known as {{mpl|2020 CD|3}} has been captured by [[Earth]]'s gravitational field and has been in orbit since 2017, becoming a [[temporary satellite|temporary]] [[natural satellite]] of Earth. The [[Minor Planet Center]] confirms the findings and says "no link to a known artificial object has been found", implying the object is an asteroid. [https://www.newscientist.com/article/2235427-earth-has-acquired-a-brand-new-moon-thats-about-the-size-of-a-car/#ixzz6F6Y9rpdp (''New Scientist'')]
